customer-jess: Hi team — our users started seeing 400s from the embeddings endpoint after we rolled a small client change. Error: 

{
  "error": "dimension mismatch: got vector length 768 but model expected 1536"
}

We only changed the client-side batching helper (we try to be clever and auto-batch single items). Anyone seen this before?

maya: hey @customer-jess — can you paste the exact request body you're sending (no auth keys)? Also which model + SDK version?

customer-jess: model: text-embed-xxl (1536). SDK: our in-house wrapper around fetch (we call it agent-lib v0.3.1). Request body (redacted):

```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-xxl",
  "input": [
    ["how to reset password"],
    "check billing",
    ["account locked"]
  ]
}
```

maya: ah ok i see a suspicious pattern — your first and third elements are arrays containing a single string, but the second is a bare string. The embeddings API expects either a single string (scalar) or an array of strings, but mixing nested arrays can lead to client libs serializing as nested vectors. That could produce a nested-array payload the server interprets as precomputed vectors instead of text.

eli: adding that when the API receives an array-of-arrays we treat it as precomputed embeddings (numbers), so if the outer element is an array of strings it might cause a parse path that later tries to cast to floats and ends up with lengths that don't match model dims.

customer-jess: oh man. That's exactly what we did — we tried to keep per-item metadata so we wrapped some inputs. Example of the wrapper output: 

```json
{"items": [{"text": "how to reset password"}, {"text": "check billing"}]}
```

But our batching translation converts to: `input: items.map(i => i.text || i)` which ended up producing mixed nesting.

maya: can you reproduce with curl? small repro please, paste both request and response (again redact tokens).

customer-jess: repro:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"text-embed-xxl","input":[["one"],"two"]}'
```

response: 400 + body: 

{
  "error": "dimension mismatch: got vector length 768 but model expected 1536"
}

maya: thanks. @devex @eng-rob fyi — customer is hitting a shape/encoding issue when client mixes nested arrays and scalars. Might be worth adding a clearer 4xx error or docs note.

devex: noted. we should add a doc snippet recommending input normalization to a flat array of strings. Also plan to add a helpful error message that says "received nested array, did you mean to pass precomputed vectors?"

eng-rob: could also be a runtime quirk: we have two code paths: (1) precomputed vectors path that expects numeric arrays length==model_dim and (2) text path that tokenizes. If the parser confuses types we can hit an attempted float cast and produce arbitrary lengths. I'll schedule an exec to tighten validation.

ops-liz: customer reported a latency spike around the same time as errors. it's probably retries from the client after 4xx? any evidence of increased request volume?

maya: logs show retries from the same IP, a small burst — looks like client retries on 4xx with backoff. Not a platform outage.

customer-jess: quick Q — what's the recommended normalization? We can change our helper quickly.

maya: normalize to: 
1) ensure top-level `input` is an array of scalars (strings) when using text embeddings; flatten any nested arrays of length-1.
2) if sending precomputed vectors, use key `vectors` (or whatever the API expects) and ensure elements are numeric arrays of length == model dimension.

Example normalization in JS: 
```js
function normalizeInputs(items) {
  return items.map(x => {
    if (Array.isArray(x) && x.length === 1 && typeof x[0] === 'string') return x[0];
    if (typeof x === 'object' && x.text) return x.text;
    return x;
  });
}
// then call embeddings with {model: 'text-embed-xxl', input: normalizeInputs(yourBatch)}
```

eli: we should also add a server-side quick-fail if any array element is mixed-type (e.g., array of strings nested) and return `400` with a clear diagnostic. I'll open a runtime PR.

eng-rob: opening ENG ticket RW-2187 to add stricter validation and better error text. Assigning to eng-runtime.

support-bot: Created ticket RW-2187 and linked thread.

customer-jess: thanks all. one last weirdness: some of our users saw embeddings with length 0 in logs — is that likely from empty string inputs?

maya: yes empty string -> embedding of length model_dim but often all zeros in some models and might look suspicious in downstream ops. Recommend filter out empty strings before calling or map them to a default placeholder like `"[empty]"` so you can distinguish true empties.

customer-jess: updated our helper and rolled to canary — errors gone. thanks for the quick help.

maya: great, closing on our side once devex adds docs + eng-runtime PR merges. :thumbsup:

eli: leaving a small note: if anyone sees `dimension mismatch` again, capture the raw JSON body (not just the parsed object) — that reveals double-encoding issues from some HTTP clients.
